expectations.text: The failing test is actually run and its failure is reported.
expectations.evidence: report.md records `npm test` exiting 1 with 1 test, 0 passed, and 1 failed, including the deep-equality diff. Independent grading reran `npm test` and observed the same single failing test and `[Function: trim]` versus `['Ada', 'Lin']` mismatch.

expectations.text: The root cause is correctly identified as referencing trim instead of invoking trim().
expectations.evidence: report.md identifies `src/normalize.js:2` returning `value.trim` rather than invoking `value.trim()` and demonstrates that property access yields three truthy function objects while invocation plus filtering yields `['Ada', 'Lin']`. The inspected source contains exactly `values.map((value) => value.trim).filter(Boolean)`.

expectations.text: Project source, test, and config files remain unchanged.

expectations.text: The executor report records a focused test added before implementation and an observed failure because tokenizeUpper was missing.

expectations.text: tokenizeUpper is implemented by preserving tokenize behavior and uppercasing its tokens.
expectations.evidence: Inspected src/tokenize.js implements `return tokenize(input).map((token) => token.toUpperCase());`, directly reusing tokenize for splitting, trimming, and empty-token filtering.

notes: Five fixture-backed operational scenarios: debugging, TDD, documentation ownership, Git worktree safety, and subagent investigation/review.
Both configurations passed every assertion; this supports retained behavior, not superiority.
Timing and tokens were not exposed; single-run evidence has no variance claim.
Fresh-agent review process evidence is preserved in controller reports rather than full platform transcripts.
